Detail: Operation Romeo commenced, an organised police crackdown in the Maoist heartland of Rolpa. Reportedly aimed at rooting out the Maoists and their sympathisers, the operation resulted in mass human rights abuses, 132 arrested, 6000 displaced, and the arbitrary detention, torture, execution and enforced disappearance of hundreds.
Keywords: security offensive, Nepal police, Rolpa, pre-conflict, human rights violations, state

Detail: Maoist leader Baburam Bhattarai submitted a 40-point demand to Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who dismissed it and traveled to India for a state visit.
Keywords: 40-point demand, ultimatum to government, state rejection of demands, Singha Durbar Kathmandu, Maoist, state

Detail: Maoists attack a police post in Holeri, Rolpa, announcing the launch of their 'people's war'.
Keywords: conflict onset, Maoist offensive, Holeri, Rolpa,  Maoist

Detail: Prime Minster Deuba convenes an all-party meeting concerning the conflict, but the issue is largely substantively dismissed.
Keywords: political dialogue, lack of political commitment, state

Detail: Dil Bahadur Ramtel (11/12), a student from Pandung, Gorkha, is shot and killed by police during protests against the arrest of a school headmaster. He is widely regarded as the first martyr of Nepal's Maoist insurgency.
Keywords: police shooting, civilian killing, school, student, Gorkha, violence, civilian, protests

Detail: The state launches a harsh police crackdown in the midwestern hills. However, police violence against civilians feeds the Maoist insurgency with fresh recruits.
Keywords: security offensive, human rights violations, civilian affected, insurgent recruitment, Rolpa, Rukum, Mid-western, state, Maoist

Detail: Maoists boycott local elections, eight people are killed in campaign violence. The government forms a taskforce to find a political solution to the conflict.
Keywords: election, political dialogue initiative, non-military response, nationwide, violence, Maoist, state

Detail: The government attempts to introduce anti-terrorism legislation through the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Control and Punishment) Act ('TADA'), but the proposed Act is withdrawn following widespread opposition from civil society groups.
Keywords: legislative attempt, civil society opposition, anti-terrorism, state

Detail: As part of the negotiation of TADA , the government publicly characterises the Maoist Insurgency as a 'terrorist' and 'disruptive' movement, signaling a shift from treating the conflict solely as a law-and-order issue toward a national security concern.
Keywords: anti-terrorism, counterterrorism, conflict securitization, Kathmandu, state

Detail: By this time, more than 50 Village Development Committees ('VDC') in Rolpa alone are under Maoist control.
Keywords: expansion, Rolpa, Maoist

Detail: Operation Kilo Sierra II: Girija Prasad (G.P.) Koirala-led government expands police counter-insurgency operations across 18 districts, marking a major escalation of the conflict. By the end of 1998, 500 people have been killed under suspicion of holding Maoist sympathies.
Keywords: security offensive, human rights violations, civilian affected, state, Maoist, civilian killing, nationwide

Detail: CPN–UML leader Yadu Gautam is assassinated by Maoist insurgents.
Keywords: assassination, Maoist, violence

Detail: Maoist insurgents start a campaign under which select enemies would be physically eliminated.
Keywords: targeted killing, violence, campaign, military campaign, maoist

Detail: Maoists strike in Kathmandu, detonating bombs at the offices of the Election Commission and Gorkhapatra, the largest circulated Nepali newspaper.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, media, state, bomb attack, violence, Maoist

Detail: Parliamentary elections are held and the Maoists call for a boycott. Krishna Prasad Bhattarai becomes prime minister and he appoints Sher Bahadur Deuba to lead a committee tasked with finding a solution to 'the Maoist problem'.
Keywords: election, conflict resolution, legislative attempt, committee,

Detail: The Government introduces Nepal Laws Relating to Internal Administration (Amendment) Bill to Parliament, aimed at strengthening powers to bring 'terrorist activities' under control. Opposition Members of the House of Representatives reject the Bill on September 21.
Keywords: counterterrorism, legislative attempt, state, parliament, Kathmandu

Detail: The Maoists expand out of the midwestern hills for the first time into central Nepal and the eastern hills.
Keywords: expansion, Maoist, midwestern, central, eastern

Detail: Maoists waylay a bus in Dolakha district carrying Polish tourists and rob them of about US$ 5,000 in cash. This is the first major incident by Maoists targeting foreign visitors.
Keywords: Maoist, Maoist offensive, civilian, Central

Detail: During commemorations of the fourth anniversary of the 'People's War', Maoist leader Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' issues a press statement saying the Maoists may now be willing to negotiate with the government to end violence, killings and abductions, if the government agrees to certain conditions.
Keywords: Maoist, political dialogue

Detail: G.P. Koirala again becomes Prime Minister after Krishna Prasad Bhattarai resigns following pressure for his inability to contain the Maoist insurgents.
Keywords: State, Parliament

Detail: Maoists use the chaos in Kathmandu to continue attacks on police posts and government offices. Police start pulling out of rural areas in the Midwest.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, violence, Nepal police, Maoist, state, Mid-western

Detail: Maoist insurgents surround a police post manned by 53 police personnel in Jajarkot district and attack with mortars and bombs. Nine policemen, seven civilians and 21 insurgents are killed in the incident.
Keywords: security offensive, human rights violations, civilian, insurgent recruitment, Rolpa, Rukum, Mid-western, state, Maoist/

Detail: Maoist leadership rejects an offer of negotiations made by the government as, in their opinion, the government failed to create the minimum favorable environment for negotiations.
Keywords: Political dialogue, state, Maoist.

Detail: Deputy PM Ram Chandra Poudel meets Maoist leader Rabindra Shrestha in Kathmandu to attempt to negotiate a solution to the conflict.
Keywords: Political dialogue, dialogue initiative, Maoist, state

Detail: Hundreds of Maoist guerrillas stormed Dunai from all sides on the night of 25 September 2001, freeing prisoners, looting Rs 50 million from the branch of Nepal Bank and abducting 12 officials. Dozens of Maoists were killed, as were 14 policemen. Home Minister Govinda Raj Joshi resigns. This incident is considered a widespread security failure which led to the establishment of the Armed Police Force - despite prior intelligence suggesting the possibility of an attack, the Royal Palace refused a request from the government to deploy the army, pointing to a gap between state police and military capability.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, violence, Nepal police, Maoist, Dolpa

Detail: Government forms special tribunal under the State Offences and Punishment Act, to prosecute crimes against the state, particularly those committed by Maoists.
Keywords: Legislative attempt, counterterrorism, conflict securitisation

Detail: Government establishes the Armed Police Force, a paramilitary force tasked with counter-insurgency operations.
Keywords: Armed Police Force, counterterrorism, counterinsurgency, state

Detail: Former King promulgates the Armed Police Ordinance intended to activate the Armed Police Force (APF) and make arrangements for its deployment against the Maoist insurgents.
Keywords: Armed Police Force, counterterrorism, counterinsurgency, state

Detail: Maoist insurgents ambush the convoy of the country's Chief Justice, Keshav Prasad Upadhyay, who narrowly escapes the attack, in Chhyasatti, Surkhet, 500km west of Kathmandu. Six others, including a judicial officer, are killed in the attack.
Keywords: Mid-western, Maoist offensive, violence, targeted killing, state, Maoist

Detail: The eve of the fifth anniversary of the commencement of the 'People's War' brings about an escalation in insurgent activities. Maoists use the anniversary to announce the Prachanda Path doctrine, the ideological line of the Maoist party drawn from Marxism-Leninism-Maoism.
Keywords: Maoist

Detail: Maoists set all documents on fire at the Bahrabise bazaar police station. They also set the Samdu police post, near Mayanglung, on fire. In another attack on security forces, the Maoists injure a policeman at the Madhumalla police station and cut off the limbs of a school teacher in Shantipur, near Gulmi.
Keywords: Maoist, Nepal police, Maoist offensive, school, human rights violations

Detail: The government and Maoist insurgents unofficially consider peace talks.
Keywords: Maoist, state, political dialogue, dialogue initiative

Detail: Prime Minister G.P. Koirala makes a fresh initiative to end the five-year old insurgency and offers to hold talks with the Maoists. Human Rights activist Tuladhar and others also involve themselves in working out the mechanism to bring the Maoist insurgents and the government to the negotiating table.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, Maoist, state

Detail: In a wave of attacks in Rukum and Dailekh, Maoists kill 70 policemen in a week and loot weapons. The paramilitary Armed Police Force is set up.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, Maoist, Nepal police, Armed Police Force, Mid-western, Far-western

Detail: In a nation-wide address, Prime Minister G.P. Koirala appeals to the Maoists to end violence and surrender weapons, while assuring them of a general amnesty.
Keywords: Maoist, state, dialogue initiative

Detail: CPN-UML calls for a three-day nation-wide general strike, which turns violent. All ten leftist parties in the country extend support to the strike.
Keywords: Protests, violence

Detail: The royal massacre occurs, resulting in the deaths of nine members of the royal family. A government-appointed inquiry confirmed Crown Prince Dipendra as the perpetrator.
Keywords: State

Detail: Prince Gyanendra, brother of Birendra is crowned King after late King Birendra's son, Dipendra––who had been declared King on June 2––succumbs to injuries sustained during the palace shooting.
Keywords: State

Detail: Nine Maoist insurgents, including five women cadres, are killed in attacks on three police outposts in Lamjung, Gulmi, and Nuwakot.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, security offensive, Nepal police, Central

Detail: Maoist insurgents set off explosions near the residence of Prime Minister G.P. Koirala at Biratnagar. However, no one is killed or injured in the incident.
Keywords: State, bomb attack, Maoist, Maoist offensive

Detail: Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister Ram Chandra Paudel resigns from the Cabinet, saying democracy in Nepal is in crisis.
Keywords: State

Detail: Prime Minister G.P. Koirala resigns. He is replaced by Sher Bahadur Deuba.
Keywords: State

Detail: Maoist insurgents declare cease-fire.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, Maoist

Detail: The government holds first talks with the Maoists.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, Maoist, state

Detail: Maoists begin attacks against public schools and declare war on alcohol.
Keywords: School, Maoist, Maoist offensive

Detail: Madhab Kumar Nepal and Bamdev Gautam meet Prachanda in Siliguri in India. At the first round of talks between the Maoists and the government, the Maoists demand abolition of constitutional monarchy, rewriting of the Constitution, and establishing an interim government to facilitate transition to a republic.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, political dialogue, state rejection of demands, Maoist, state, ultimatum to government

Detail: A second round of talks between the government and the insurgents ends inconclusively as the Maoists insist on the formation of a Republic and setting up of a Constituent Assembly to review the Constitution.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, political dialogue, state rejection of demands, ultimatum to government

Detail: Deuba proposes postponing elections because of the security situation. King Gyanendra dismisses him, assumes executive authority and sets up a government of technocrats.
Keywords: State

Detail: The Defence Ministry announces that the US government has made a commitment to supply Nepal with 10 modern, fully armed military helicopters to 'fight terrorism'.
Keywords: State, military campaign

Detail: A third round of talks between the government and Maoist insurgents ends in deadlock. Government insists on making changes to the Constitution now in force to accommodate Maoist demands, but refuses to abrogate it. The Maoists stick to their demand that a Constituent Assembly be convened to further ensure people’s rights. Significantly, the Maoists drop their demand for a Republic.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, political dialogue, state rejection of demands, ultimatum to government

Detail: Maoist insurgents trash the ongoing truce and during the night, attack the Army barracks in Ghorai, Dang district, killing 14 soldiers and injuring 30 more. Insurgents announce the formation of a central People’s Revolutionary Government with Babu Ram Bhattarai as Chief Convenor of the Maoist parallel government. Insurgents attack the airport in Surkhet and blow up a privately-owned helicopter, damaging two more.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, military campaign, Moist, state, violence, bomb attack, Mid-Western

Detail: The king declares a state of emergency in the country and orders the deployment of troops against the Maoists.
Keywords: State, conflict securitisation

Detail: Terrorism Ordinance 2001 passed, expanding government powers to declare and address terrorism.
Keywords: Legislative attempt, counterterrorism, conflict securitisation, state
